==English==

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:-<ety:inh<ang:andlang>>|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂en-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, from {{inh|en|ang|andlang}}, from prefix {{m|ang|and-}} + {{m|ang|lang||long}}. {{doublet|en|endlong}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{a|en|UK}}
** {{IPA|en|/əˈlɒŋ/|a=RP}}
** {{IPA|en|/əˈlæŋ/|a=Northumbrian}}

** {{IPA|en|/əˈlɑŋ/|a=cot-caught}}
** {{IPA|en|/əˈlɔŋ/|a=non-cot-caught}}

* {{rhymes|en|ɒŋ|ɔŋ|s=2}}

===Preposition===
{{en-head|prep}}

# By the [[length]] of; in a line with the length of; [[lengthwise]] next to.
#: {{ux|en|Water whished '''along''' the boat as we rowed upstream.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1892|author=Sir {{w|Arthur Conan Doyle}}|chapter=w:The Adventure of the Copper Beeches|title=w:The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes| page=294| url=http://books.google.com/books?id=buc0AAAAMAAJ&pg=PA294&lpg=PA294| passage=They were waiting for me in the drawing-room, which is a very large room, stretching '''along''' the entire front of the house, with three long windows reaching down to the floor}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|page=52|passage=My hopes wa'n't disappointed. I never saw clams thicker than they was '''along''' them inshore flats. I filled my dreener in no time, and then it come to me that 'twouldn't be a bad idee to get a lot more, take 'em with me to Wellmouth, and peddle 'em out. Clams was fairly scarce over that side of the bay and ought to fetch a fair price.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1990
|chapter=Transport and Communications
|title=The Geographical Digest 1990-91
|url=https://archive.org/details/geograpicaldiges0000unse/
|location=Oxford
|publisher=w:Heinemann Educational Books
|ISBN=0435349570
|OCLC=220955535
|page=106
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/geograpicaldiges0000unse/page/106/
|column=2
|text=The first 80 km section of the Hyesan to Kanggye link was opened on 22.12.88 to follow the Chinese border '''along''' the Amnok-gang river valley.}}
# In a line with, with a [[progressive]] [[motion]] on; [[onward]] on; [[forward]] on.
#* {{RQ:KJV|Samuel 1|6|2|passage=The kine{{...}}went '''along''' the highway.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1892|author=Sir {{w|Arthur Conan Doyle}}|chapter=w:The Boscombe Valley Mystery|title=w:The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes| page=93| url=http://books.google.com/books?id=buc0AAAAMAAJ&pg=PA93| passage=Swiftly and silently he made his way '''along''' the track which ran through the meadows.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|page=304|passage=We tiptoed into the house, up the stairs and '''along''' the hall to the door of the room where the Professor had been spending so much of his time.}}

===Adverb===
{{en-adv|-}}

# In [[company]]; [[together]].
#: {{ux|en|John played the piano and everyone sang '''along'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian
|date=June 26, 2017
|author=Alexis Petridis
|title=Glastonbury 2017 verdict: Radiohead, Foo Fighters, Lorde, Stormzy and more
|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/jun/26/glastonbury-2017-verdict-radiohead-foo-fighters-lorde-stormzy-and-more
|passage= From The Best of You to The Pretender, their own material invariably came equipped with huge choruses designed to be bellowed '''along''' to; they covered Another One Bites the Dust and Under Pressure; they gave every impression of being willing to play all night were it not for the curfew.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261012112015/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/jun/26/glastonbury-2017-verdict-radiohead-foo-fighters-lorde-stormzy-and-more|archivedate=12 October 2026}}
# [[onward|Onward]], [[forward]], with progressive action.
#: {{ux|en|Don't stop here. Just move '''along'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|page=18|passage=I stumbled '''along''' through the young pines and huckleberry bushes. Pretty soon I struck into a sort of path that, I cal'lated, might lead to the road I was hunting for. It twisted and turned, and, the first thing I knew, made a sudden bend around a bunch of bayberry scrub and opened out into a big clear space like a lawn.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1989|month=May|volume=175|number=5|title=Braving the Northwest Passage|author=Jeff MacInnis|page=588
|text=Here in Franklin Bay during our first season we hurtle '''along''' at 20 knots, dodging ice floes littering the surface.}}
